Actually, let me ask you three things. Okay, first, what would you do if you found a snake in your
house? You call somebody to catch it and get it out of there, right? I mean, you wouldn't just say,
well, I guess I live with a snake now? Of course not, you'd get rid of it. Okay, second question,
what if you found bugs crawling around in your bed? What would you do? You'd spray them, you'd
kill them, you'd clean everything up and get them out of your bed? What do you do when you find out
there are dust mites living in your bed? Well, you capture them and get rid of them too, right?
Oh wait, you can't, because you can't even see them. So what are you supposed to do? Well,
that's the problem. You basically just accept it. You say, okay, I guess dust mites live in my bed
now. And instead of getting rid of them, you just try to make living with them a little easier.
You wash your sheets in hot water, you vacuum more often, you run an air purifier, you take anti-histamines,
maybe you buy a special mattress cover. And listen, maybe some of that helps. But you're still
basically saying, you guys can stay in my bed, I'll just keep dealing with everything around you.
Because really, what other choice do you have? You can't see them, you can't catch them,
so you just lend a lid with them. Well, what if I told you, that's not true? What if you could
capture dust mites? What if you could trap them, pick them up and throw them away, just like you
would with any other pest? Well now you can. These are called capture kites, and the way they work
is actually pretty clever. Scientists discovered that dust mites use chemical signals called
pheromones to find one another. One of those signals is called narrow propionate. To a dust
mite, that signal basically says, hey, other dust mites are over here.
Capture cards use that signal as a lure, so instead of sitting there and hoping a dust mite
accidentally walks onto the card, the card draws them toward it. The mites follow the signal,
they move toward the card, and once they're inside, an adhesive layer traps them so they can't call
back out. You just place the cards near your mattress and pillows as directed, and let them work.
No sprays, no insecticides, nothing to plug in. Then, when it's time to replace the card,
you pick it up and throw it away. Mites and all. That's it.
So now, you don't have to treat dust mites like invisible roommates you're stuck with in
life. You may not be able to see them, but now you can capture them, you can remove them,
and you can finally do more than just clean around them and hope for the best.
